clue.text: Article by girl about unknown region of Greece

parts.note: the definite article is the word the

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the girl's word is read backwards

parts.note: a lass is a girl
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A grammar note: an article stands beside a girl's name, wrapped around some mystery, all for a Greek place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl' is a common word for her here, not a name; Y as the unknown is an algebra convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Thessaly is a historic region in central Greece, a straightforward geographical example.

clue.text: Commotion requiring action?

definitions.meaning: a fuss or kerfuffle, the noun sense
a task described as still to be done, the phrase read literally

explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss or commotion; a job still to do is one needing action, as on a list of tasks.

clue.text: Lamb having tail clipped was poorly reared

indicators.note: in a down clue reared means raised up, so the letters read from bottom to top
the last letter is cut off, as a tail is trimmed

parts.note: to have ailed is to have been poorly

explanation.surface: A lamb that had its tail docked was sickly while being raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having tail clipped' turns AILED into AILE, and 'reared' turns that upward into the answer. Charles Lamb wrote his essays under this pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb, the English essayist, signed his Essays under the pseudonym Elia.

clue.text: Article on scandium and yttrium must be cut

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits below it, so the article comes last

parts.note: Sc is the chemical symbol for scandium
Y is the chemical symbol for yttrium
the definite article is the word the

explanation.surface: A chemistry write-up on two elements is too long and must be trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To scythe grass or corn is to cut it with a long curved blade.

clue.text: Bound to have unforeseen consequences

parts.note: reads as a prediction that something is certain to backfire, but bound is a jump, and this is one taken blind whose outcome cannot be foreseen

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a risky step taken without knowing what will follow, a jump made blind.

clue.text: Backward area provided much fibrous material

indicators.note: backward tells us the whole run of pieces is read from the end to the start

parts.note: if means provided that
far, as in far better, means much

explanation.surface: A remote district supplied a great quantity of fibrous stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'Backward', turns the whole three-piece run, not just the area.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is fibre from a palm's leaves, used for weaving baskets and tying plants.

clue.text: Incorporate college?

parts.note: split as in-corporate, the word suggests taking in every body, so a college that admits everyone, every person counted as a body

explanation.walkthrough: ALL SOULS is a college of Oxford University; 'corporate' hints at bodies, and souls are people.
explanation.definitionFit: All Souls is an Oxford college, and its name taken literally means every person, every body included.

clue.text: Sole trader — he's forming new organisation

indicators.note: a new organisation of the letters means they are rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: A man running his own business explains that he is setting up a fresh company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole trader' looks like the business term for a one-person firm; here sole is the flatfish, so it is someone who trades fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishmonger trades in fish, sole among them, so the business phrase is read as a fish seller.

clue.text: Gobsmacked — one's dropped by university!

parts.note: Aston is a university in Birmingham
the Roman numeral I is one
to shed is to drop, as a tree drops leaves

explanation.surface: A student is astounded to learn they have been thrown out by their university.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has', a link: one (I) has shed, beside ASTON, Birmingham's Aston University.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobsmacked is British slang for utterly amazed, a synonym of astounded or stunned.

clue.text: Where Friesians may be seen on Friday going out on a limb

indicators.note: going out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: Someone spots black-and-white cows on a Friday night out, having gone out on a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' tempts as a date night, but it signals the anagram; 'on a' is a link. Friesians are cattle, not people from Friesland.
explanation.definitionFit: Friesians are black-and-white dairy cattle, so a farm producing milk is where you would find them.

clue.text: Big business has to limit annual turnover

indicators.note: turnover suggests the letters are turned over and mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A large firm is told to cap its yearly sales figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like the company's sales; it is the anagram signal for TO LIMIT ANNUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A multinational is a large company operating in many countries, so big business in the corporate sense.

clue.text: Composer heard in recital?

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is spoken, and a name of the same sound is written

parts.note: a recital of things is a list of them, an enumeration

explanation.surface: A composer's piece is performed at a concert recital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recital' looks like a concert, but here it is a listing of items.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian Romantic pianist and composer.

clue.text: Odd item on a shelf — it has legs for arms

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange object sits on a shelf, with legs where its arms should be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' is not limbs but a coat of arms: the island's emblem is three armoured legs. The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The island's coat of arms and flag show the triskelion, three running legs joined at the hip.

clue.text: Cause a fight after bishop's call

indicators.note: the fight comes after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to ring someone is to call them on the phone
a bout is a boxing match, a fight

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out after the bishop telephones.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about something is to cause it to happen, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: By the way, they are replacing broken sets

definitions.text: By the way, they are replacing broken sets

parts.words: By the way, they are replacing broken sets
parts.note: read as a casual aside, but by the way means beside the road, and these are stones laid along it in place of damaged paving setts

explanation.walkthrough: A sett is a squared paving stone; British 'kerb' is the American 'curb'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerbstones edge a road, lying along the way, and can be laid where old paving setts have cracked.

clue.text: Dance that's authentic, so it's said

indicators.note: so it's said tells us the word is spoken and a same-sounding word is written

parts.note: real means authentic, genuine

explanation.surface: A dance is genuine, or so people claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance.

clue.text: Youths multiplying within seconds

indicators.note: within means the multiplying word goes inside the seconds

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second, so two seconds give two of them
tripling is multiplying by three

explanation.surface: Young people are breeding rapidly in a matter of seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIPLING sits between the two S letters given by 'seconds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Striplings are young men, adolescents not yet fully grown, so youths.

clue.text: Resent move to imprison European monarch

indicators.note: to imprison means to hold inside, so the other pieces sit within

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: Someone resents a plan to jail a European king.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge someone something is to resent their having it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: For example, silver belt on male model

indicators.note: model as a verb means shape, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A silver belt is fashioned to sit on a male model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a fashion model, but it is the anagram signal for BELT ON MALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver, gold and platinum are noble metals, which resist corrosion and oxidation.

clue.text: Worker entertaining Durham's first historian

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the bee holds the letter inside

parts.note: a worker is a bee, the commonest crossword worker

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word Durham's

explanation.surface: A labourer entertains the first historian at Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: The Venerable Bede's tomb is in Durham Cathedral, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede wrote the Ecclesiastical History of the English People, so he is the father of English history.

clue.text: What is lumberjack doing? What about branch?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: eh is an exclamation meaning what, asking someone to repeat
a wing is a branch of an organisation or building

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the lumberjack is up to and what about the branch.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'What' belongs to the definition; the second is the exclamation that 'about' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewing is chopping wood with an axe, the lumberjack's activity.

clue.text: Directive for missionaries or substitutes?

definitions.meaning: an instruction to change the local people
other options or replacements, the plural noun

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it tells missionaries to change local people; as one word it means options or replacements.

clue.text: Note setter's modus operandi

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
MO is the abbreviation for modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: A note describes the crossword setter's working method.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a short written note, from memorandum.

clue.text: Part for Moira Shearer as a tennis player

indicators.note: part for means a portion of the words given, so the answer sits inside them

explanation.surface: A ballet star is offered a film role as a tennis player.
explanation.walkthrough: Moira Shearer was a Scottish ballerina and actress; Arthur Ashe won Wimbledon in 1975.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe was an American tennis champion, winner of three Grand Slam singles titles.

clue.text: Had some sudden worry or upset

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the letters are read backwards
some means only a portion of the words, so the letters lie inside

explanation.surface: Someone suffered a sudden fear or distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' finds DENWO across 'sudden worry'; 'upset' turns it round. 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have owned something is to have had it in one's possession.

clue.text: Family repeatedly getting letter revealing abnormality

indicators.note: repeatedly means the family word appears more than once, here twice

parts.note: kin are family, relatives
ess is the spelled-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: A family keeps receiving letters that expose something odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinkiness is peculiarity or deviance, especially in sexual taste, so an abnormality.

clue.text: Elephant given half of bitter with Welsh water in it

indicators.note: in it means the river goes inside the half-word
half of picks out the last three letters of the word bitter

parts.note: the Usk is a river in south Wales

explanation.surface: An elephant is given half a pint of bitter mixed with Welsh water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes the back half of bitter, and 'in it' sets the Welsh river inside that half.
explanation.definitionFit: A tusker is an elephant or other animal with prominent tusks.

clue.text: European, after decline, means to raise standard

indicators.note: the European comes after the decline in the answer

parts.note: to flag is to decline or tire
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A European, after a downturn, finds a way to raise standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a level of quality, but it is a flag, which a pole raises.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagpole is the pole on which a standard, or flag, is hoisted.
